queue.brief: #147 measured the allotments as monoculture BY CONSTRUCTION — species per plot 1.000 over 69,008 sown samples — and wrote the invariant into `plotCrop()` along with the successor read for the day it stops holding. #152 then built the hand that could stop it, but `plotAct()`'s sow rung still fills bare cells with `plotCrop()` itself, so the plot stays one crop (the comment at ~line 3996 says exactly that). Let a hand sow a DIFFERENT crop into a fallow cell — a holder inter-cropping, which is what the rung is for — and then make `plotCrop()` answer for the plot's MAJORITY, which is the read #147 left ready. One predicate, one definition: every downstream reader of plotCrop must be walked, not assumed.
queue.successLooksLike: Over a year x 3 seeds some plots hold two species (species/plot above 1.000 — say what it is), the beans still put their canes up on the plots that are actually beans, and the glasshouse crop still never appears outside the span.
queue.avoid: Do not break the winter invariant #147 measured: tender crops in the open must still reach stage 3 zero times in deep winter, against hardy 21,474 and glass 10,191. Do not make every plot mixed — a plot that stays one crop is still the common case; the finding is that it has stopped being universal. And if a downstream reader of plotCrop turns out to want the FIRST cell rather than the majority, say which and why rather than changing them all.
